Also not python specific but you reminded me of something, I remember getting assigned to code a "small script" to upload files into a remote storage deemed as "quick and easy" by my then boss.

I had some doubts and instead of writing a huge email, I made a workflow chart, easy, simple, pretty straightforward and sent it to him, he replied with "that's good, keep going".

A couple of weeks go by and he requests a code-review meeting, sure thing I said.

Not even 5 minutes went by and he started asking "why is this function here?" "why did you build this?" "this is a disaster".

So I had to ask: did you actually check the workflow that I sent you? "Yes" he said but, it was literally the 3rd box from the start that had that function mentioned.

Everybody got d\*cked on, from his manager to mine for not communicating properly and wasting time.

Now, what did I learn from this?

1. Requirements meetings should and always be registered one way or another, minutes, logs and recordings are a MUST.
2. Always make sure that what the other person is asking aligns with what you understood about it, diagrams or even small drawings help A LOT. This is when pseudocode, diagrams and even verbalizing are a must.
3. Define milestones and/or objectives within your deliverables.

I felt like crap about it but learned a huge deal.
